info.name: TCGplayer API v1.39.0
info.description:
Merged from TCGplayer's per-endpoint OpenAPI definitions at https://docs.tcgplayer.com/reference (retrieved 2026-10-08). Each operation's `x-docs-url` links its source page.

**Access:** TCGplayer states it is no longer granting new API access; existing keys only.

## Additions to the official definitions
- `servers` adds the `/{version}` prefix shown in the Getting Started guide (`https://api.tcgplayer.com/[VERSION]/catalog/categories`); the reference definitions list only `https://api.tcgplayer.com`.
- `POST /token` and `securitySchemes` are hand-written from the Getting Started and Store Authorization guides; the reference definitions declare no security.
- `/token` and `/app/authorize/{authCode}` use the unversioned root, per the guides.
- Get ProductList By Id / By Key merged into one operation (same URL template).

## Auth flow
1. `POST /token` with client credentials → bearer token (`Authorization: bearer <token>`).
2. Store access: store generates an authorization code → `POST /app/authorize/{authCode}` → `AuthorizationKey` (ACCESS_TOKEN). Request a new token via `POST /token` with header `X-Tcg-Access-Token: <ACCESS_TOKEN>`.
3. `GET /stores/self` with the store-scoped token → store identity / storeKey. (The guide shows this URL without a version prefix; whether it requires one is unverified.)

## Using this collection
Set `publicKey` and `privateKey`, then send **Authentication → Request a Bearer Token**; its test script saves `bearerToken`. For store-scoped calls, set `accessToken` and `storeKey`, enable the `X-Tcg-Access-Token` header on the token request, and resend it.

header.description: Optional store ACCESS_TOKEN (AuthorizationKey) for store-scoped access.

request.description:
Exchange PUBLIC_KEY / PRIVATE_KEY for a bearer token. To act on a contracted store, also send the store's ACCESS_TOKEN (the `AuthorizationKey` from POST /app/authorize/{authCode}) in the `X-Tcg-Access-Token` header; the returned token is then store-scoped. Tokens are valid until `.expires`; cache and refresh near expiry. Hand-written from the Getting Started and Store Authorization guides (not in TCGplayer's reference definitions).

Docs: https://docs.tcgplayer.com/docs/getting-started

request.description:
If a store's status is either Live or Hold - User Request then this action may be called to flip the store between the
two.  When the store is Live, it's inventory is visible in the marketplace.  When the store is not Live, it's inventory
is hidden from the marketplace.  Stores may voluntarily hide their inventory by switching their status to Hold - User
Request.  There are other statuses that TCGplayer can put the store in that wil cause it's inventory to be hidden from
the marketplace.  Stores cannot put themselves in or take themselves out of these statuses.  Only a TCGplayer admin or
customer service rep can interact with stores with these statuses.

Docs: https://docs.tcgplayer.com/reference/stores_setstorestatus-1
